info.title: Romdoul OCR API
info.description:
Khmer document OCR over plain HTTP. Upload an image or PDF and get back text, layout regions, tables, and translations.

**Three OCR engines answer the same five endpoints.** Swap the path prefix to switch engine — request and response shapes are identical:

| Prefix | Engine | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/api` | Khmer Parsing API (cloud GPU) | Best Khmer accuracy, translation, confidence scores. Default. |
| `/api-vllm` | Surya OCR 2 (self-hosted GPU) | Private processing, adjustable render DPI. No translation. |
| `/api-lens` | Google Lens | Fast general text. No confidence, no table structure. |

### Access
No API key is required — if you have the endpoint, you can call it. Usage is **rate limited** instead: **120 requests/minute per client, bursting to 40**. Health checks get a looser budget. Exceed it and you get `429` with a `Retry-After` header; back off and continue.

### Versioning
All paths are served under **`/v1`** — `https://romdoulocr.netlify.app/v1/api/ocr-image`. Build against `/v1` and a future breaking change will ship as `/v2` without touching you.

### Idempotency
Any POST accepts an optional **`Idempotency-Key`** header (any unique string — a UUID per source document works well). The first call runs normally; a repeat with the same key within **24 hours** replays the stored response instead of re-running OCR. Use it so a dropped connection or a pipeline retry never double-spends GPU time or produces a second, subtly different result. The response carries `X-Idempotency-Replay: HIT` when it was replayed.

### Errors
Every failure returns `{ "error": { "code", "message" }, "detail" }`. Branch on the stable `error.code` — never on `detail`, which is prose meant for humans.

### Practical notes
- Send **one page per request** and run pages in parallel: it stays inside the ~26 s gateway ceiling, gives per-page progress, and fails narrowly on a bad page.
- The cloud engine sleeps when idle; the first call after a quiet period can take ~22 s. Call `/v1/api/health` before a batch to absorb that once.
- `full_text` is occasionally an empty string even when regions contain text — fall back to joining `pages[].regions[].text`.
- Image fields (`crop_base64`, `debug_image`) are **raw base64**; prepend `data:image/png;base64,` yourself.
- Retry `502`/`504` once with backoff (send the same `Idempotency-Key` — it's free if the first attempt actually landed). Never retry a `4xx` other than `429`.

get.description: Cheap readiness probe. `200` means the engine will accept work. May take up to ~22 s on a cold start.

post.description: Returns the plain text of one image. No layout or structure — use `/parse-pdf` if you need either.

Full document extraction. Returns every page with its layout regions — headings, paragraphs, tables, figures — each with text, a bounding box, and a confidence score.

The `files` field is **plural** and repeatable: send it more than once to merge several inputs into a single document with renumbered pages.

post.summary: Extract a document and translate it
post.description: Identical to `/parse-pdf`, plus `translated_text` on the response.

Returns rows, columns and cells — each cell with its grid position, text, bounding box and confidence, enough to rebuild the table as CSV or a spreadsheet.

When no table is detected you get the page text as a single-column grid rather than an empty result.

get.description: Returns `503` with `models_loaded: false` when the GPU service is unreachable. This engine depends on a machine that is not always online — fall back to `/api` on `503`.

post.description: Images are preprocessed (deskew, upscale, sharpen) before recognition to meet the model's minimum input quality on old or blurry scans.
Accepted for contract compatibility, but this engine cannot translate — `translated_text` is always `null`. Use `/api` or `/api-lens` for translation.
`confidence` is always `0` — this engine does not report one.
Words are grouped into lines by vertical proximity; one region per line. Region confidence is synthetic.

post.summary: Extract a document and translate it

post.description: Lens has no table model. A grid is reconstructed from word geometry — rows by vertical proximity, columns by horizontal whitespace gaps — and falls back to a single-column line list when no columns are detected.

get.description:
Every engine's liveness in one call, so you do not have to poll three `/health` endpoints to pick a backend.

Always returns **HTTP 200**, even when `status` is `"down"` — a non-200 here would be indistinguishable from the status service itself failing, which is exactly the ambiguity you are polling to resolve. **Branch on the `status` field in the body, never on the HTTP code.**

Per-engine `state`:

| `state` | `up` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `up` | `true` | Answering normally. Send work here. |
| `warming` | `true` | Missed the probe deadline but answered recently — almost always the cloud engine scaling from zero. Usable; expect a slow first request. |
| `not_ready` | `false` | Reachable, but reports its models are not loaded. |
| `down` | `false` | Unreachable, or failing for longer than the cold-start grace window. |

The rollup is `ok` only when **every** engine is `up`; `degraded` when at least one engine is usable but not all are fast; `down` when none are usable.

Results are cached for a few seconds (`cache_ttl_s`), so polling this endpoint is cheap. `X-Status-Cache` reports `HIT`, `MISS`, or `STALE`.

**Limitation:** this endpoint is served from the same host as the self-hosted engines. It tells you *which engine to use while the service is reachable* — it cannot tell you the service is down. If `/v1/status` does not answer at all, treat the whole deployment as unavailable.

200.description: Current status of every engine (returned even when engines are down)

X-Status-Cache.description: Whether this answer came from the short-lived cache.

post.description:
The upload is accepted and a job created immediately — OCR runs in the background, so this returns in milliseconds no matter how large the document.

PDFs are split and processed ONE PAGE PER REQUEST with bounded concurrency, then merged back in page order with `page_number` renumbered 1..N. A page that keeps failing is recorded and the job finishes as `partial` rather than dying.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` and a repeat submission returns the SAME `job_id` instead of queueing duplicate work — this is what makes pipeline retries safe.

parameters.name: concurrency
parameters.description: Pages in flight for this job (clamped to 1..8).

requestBody.description: Multipart upload. Field name is **`files`** (plural, repeatable).

get.description: Poll until `status` is terminal (`succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `cancelled`). A few seconds between polls is plenty.

delete.description: Cancels the work if it is still running, then removes the job's stored state and result files.

get.description:
Available once the job reaches a terminal state. For `parse-pdf` modes this is a single merged DocumentResult covering every page; for `ocr-image` / `parse-table` it is a list, one entry per input.

A `partial` job still returns a result — failed pages appear as placeholders carrying `error` and `error_code`, so page numbering stays aligned with the source document.

409.description: Job has not finished yet — keep polling

post.description:
Translates TEXT — it does no OCR. Useful for translating text you already extracted without paying for a second OCR pass.

Takes **JSON, not multipart**. Send Khmer as UTF-8; a mis-encoded body comes back as `?????` in `source_text`, which is the quickest way to spot the problem.

Cloud engine only — the self-hosted engines do not implement it.

Direction is whatever you pass in `source_lang` / `target_lang`.

example.text: ព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា

UseCtc.name: use_ctc
UseCtc.description: CTC decoder. Recommended for Khmer — the autoregressive decoder can fall into repetition loops on noisy scans.

DetectLayout.name: detect_layout
DetectLayout.description: Detect layout regions. Turn off to force a single whole-page read (useful for signs and photos).

DetectLines.name: detect_lines
DetectLines.description: Emit per-line bounding boxes inside each region.

RowTolerance.name: row_tolerance
RowTolerance.description: Pixel slack when grouping cells into rows. Raise it for skewed scans.

Dpi.name: dpi
Dpi.description: Render resolution for the self-hosted engine: 96 draft, 150 default, 300 for small print. Ignored by other engines.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional. Any unique string (a UUID per source document works well). A repeat within 24 h replays the stored response instead of re-running OCR, so retries never double-spend GPU time. Response carries `X-Idempotency-Replay: HIT` when replayed.

file.description: PNG, JPG, WEBP, BMP or TIFF

MultiFile.description: Multipart upload. Field name is **`files`** (plural, repeatable).

files.description: PDF or image files. Repeat the field to merge several into one document.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request — check the upload field name (`file` singular vs `files` plural)

TooLarge.description: Upload exceeds 100 MB — split the document

BadGateway.description: The engine failed. Retry once with backoff.

Unavailable.description: Engine not ready (GPU loading or offline). Poll `/health`, or fall back to `/api`.

Timeout.description: Upstream timed out — send fewer pages per request

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded (120 req/min per client, burst 40). Back off and retry.

message.description: What went wrong and what to do about it.

detail.description: Human-readable prose. Do NOT branch on this.

error.message: Too many requests. Retry after the Retry-After interval.

confidence.description: 0–1. Always 0 on the Google Lens engine.

example.text: ព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា

BoundingBox.description: Four corners in page-pixel space, clockwise from top-left — a rotated region keeps its true shape.

crop_base64.description: RAW base64 PNG (no data: prefix) for picture/figure regions

full_text.description: May be an empty string even when regions contain text — fall back to joining region text.

StatusResponse.description: Aggregate liveness of every OCR engine.

status.description: `ok` = every engine is up and fast. `degraded` = at least one engine is usable, but not all are fast. `down` = no engine is usable.

generated_at.description: When this snapshot was measured (UTC). May be up to `cache_ttl_s` old.

cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds this result is reused before a fresh fan-out. Polling faster than this returns a cached answer.

prefix.description: Path prefix to call this engine on, e.g. `/api-lens`. Append it to the server URL.

up.description: Whether it is worth sending work here. True for both `up` and `warming`.

state.description: `warming` means the engine missed the probe deadline but answered recently — usually a cold start, not an outage.

latency_ms.description: Round-trip time of the health probe. On a failed probe this is the time spent before giving up, not a service latency.

http_status.description: HTTP status the engine's own /health returned; null when it could not be reached.

models_loaded.description: As reported by the engine's /health. Null when unknown.

detail.description: Human-readable context — the engine's health message, or why the probe failed. Do NOT branch on this.

status.description: `partial` means the job finished but at least one page failed — the result is still usable.

text.description: Text to translate. Khmer must be sent as UTF-8.

source_lang.description: Optional on the directional endpoints, which set it themselves.

example.source_text: ព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា
